finding: No resting run recorded in this repository has ever applied either physiological preload. Every one started from a force-free cortex and force-free ERM tethers against a positive 40 Pa turgor -- the configuration the driver's own docstring states has no force-balanced equilibrium and gives as the reason no inner solver converges.

evidence_mechanism.why_this_is_decisive: each ledger key is written ONLY when its preload runs, and the record's ledger IS cell.ledger, so the key's absence is a witness to non-application rather than an absence of logging

cortex_prestrain_is_cli_unreachable.consequence: no CLI-driven run could have applied cortex hoop pre-tension even if asked to

what_the_driver_says_about_this_state.driver.py:235-240: At build each ERM rest length equals its formation length, so every tether is force-free and the membrane carries the full turgor pressure unbalanced ... a relaxed cortex plus a positive turgor is not a valid resting baseline (PI physiological-baseline rule) -- there is no force-balanced equilibrium there, which is why no inner solver converges from it.
what_the_driver_says_about_this_state.driver.py:24-26: if the membrane/cortex is not equilibrated at the Young-Laplace preload, NG-3 and inner_converged remain false.

reconciles_rather_than_contradicts_d71f5: preload_mechanically_feasible_upper_bound is a CAPACITY field -- whether 40,962 tethers COULD hold 40 Pa if pre-tensioned -- not a record of whether they WERE. Subdiv 6 made the shell capable and left it unloaded: every tether still at force-free formation length. So 'a feasible shell does not descend either' is what this predicts, and ffn-cellsim-45's refutation of the infeasibility hypothesis stands: it refuted the right thing, and the capacity ratio was never the live variable.
NOT_CLAIMED: that applying the preload makes the residual descend -- untested, and it is the decisive control
that no equilibrium exists -- that is the CODE's claim, resting on a physical argument (a force-free cortex carries no tension so it cannot hold turgor), not a measurement taken here
any statement about the operator conclusion, which this neither supports nor refutes
decisive_control_not_run: one resting run with the preload ON, same binary criterion declared before launch (DESCENDS iff candidate < start), everything else fixed. Needs the card and PI approval; not launched by this session.

the_control_that_was_already_in_the_repo.reading: With the turgor load off the explicit solver DESCENDS; with it on the same solver at the same scale diverges. The sign of the step flips with the load, not with the solver. This does not show convergence -- inner_converged is False in both and one step at -0.04% is not a converged solve -- but it locates the failure in the LOAD rather than in the iteration, and the load is unbalanced precisely because neither preload was ever applied.

five_solvers_are_not_five_failures.reading: explicit, anderson and analytic_implicit land on the IDENTICAL candidate 1.763638. The line search is doing its job -- it rejects every accelerated proposal as worse and falls back to the matched explicit update -- so this is ONE failure mode observed three times, not three independent solvers failing. block_descent and rkc1 are simply worse. Counting these as five independent negative results overstates the evidence.
